pinyin: jīng cǐ shì biàn, yì wú zài rǔ
literal: undergo · this · world · upheaval, duty · no · again · disgrace
natural: having lived through this upheaval, I cannot bear to be disgraced again

meaning.en: The closing words of Wang Guowei's suicide note: after such upheaval, honour allows no further humiliation.
meaning.zh: 王国维遗书中的名句：经历了这场世道巨变，按道义不能再受屈辱。

equivalents: I can bear no further humiliation
death before further disgrace

examples.zh: 读到“经此世变，义无再辱”，学生沉默了很久。
examples.en: Reading 'after this upheaval, honour permits no further disgrace', the students fell silent for a long time.

examples.zh: 讲座谈到王国维之死，引用了“经此世变，义无再辱”这句遗言。
examples.en: The lecture on Wang Guowei's death quoted his last words, 'after this upheaval, honour permits no further disgrace'.

story.en: Wang Guowei drowned himself in Kunming Lake at the Summer Palace in June 1927; his note begins '五十之年，只欠一死。经此世变，义无再辱。'
story.zh: 1927年6月，王国维在颐和园昆明湖自沉，遗书开头写道：“五十之年，只欠一死。经此世变，义无再辱。”

usage.en: A quoted line, solemn and literary. Used only when discussing Wang Guowei's death (1927) and the fate of scholars in times of upheaval; not for everyday use. Interpretations of his motives differ.
usage.zh: 引用的名句，庄重、书面。多用于谈论王国维之死（1927年）和乱世中的学人命运，不用于日常口语。对其死因的解释不一。

text: 阐旧邦以辅新命，极高明而道中庸
pinyin: chǎn jiù bāng yǐ fǔ xīn mìng, jí gāo míng ér dào zhōng yōng
literal: elucidate · old · state · to · support · new · mandate, reach · lofty · brilliant · and · follow · the mean
natural: illuminate the old nation to support its new mission; reach the heights yet walk the middle way

meaning.en: Feng Youlan's self-composed couplet: renew the ancient tradition to serve a nation's new destiny, and pursue the highest insight while keeping to the Doctrine of the Mean.
meaning.zh: 冯友兰自撰对联：阐发古老的传统以辅助国家的新使命，追求极高的智慧而又遵循中庸之道。

equivalents: renew the old to serve the new
aim high, walk the middle way

examples.zh: 书房里挂着一副对联：阐旧邦以辅新命，极高明而道中庸。
examples.en: A couplet hung in the study: 'illuminate the old nation to support its new mission; reach the heights yet walk the middle way'.

examples.zh: 他在讲座结尾引用了“阐旧邦以辅新命，极高明而道中庸”，勉励青年学者。
examples.en: He ended the lecture with 'illuminate the old nation…', encouraging young scholars.

story.en: Feng Youlan wrote this couplet for himself in his later years, drawing on the Book of Songs ('Zhou is an old state, yet its mandate is new') and the Doctrine of the Mean.
story.zh: 冯友兰晚年自撰此联，化用《诗经》“周虽旧邦，其命维新”和《中庸》“极高明而道中庸”。

usage.en: Feng Youlan's own couplet, composed late in life (reported as the 1980s). It reworks two classical phrases: 周虽旧邦，其命维新 (《诗经·大雅·文王》) and 极高明而道中庸 (《中庸》). Quoted as an emblem of renewing tradition; literary.
usage.zh: 冯友兰自撰联，作于晚年（一般说是1980年代）。化用两处经典：“周虽旧邦，其命维新”（《诗经·大雅·文王》）和“极高明而道中庸”（《中庸》）。常作传统创新的写照，书面语。

pinyin: zhào zhe jiǎng, jiē zhe jiǎng
natural: speak by the book; speak on from where it left off

meaning.en: Feng Youlan's distinction: merely repeating a tradition ('speaking along with it') versus building on it and carrying it further ('speaking on from it').
meaning.zh: 冯友兰的区分：只复述前人是“照着讲”，在前人基础上继续发展才是“接着讲”。

equivalents: not just repeat but build on
carry the tradition forward

examples.zh: 做学问既要照着讲，接着讲更重要，不能只停在复述。
examples.en: In scholarship one speaks along with the old, but continuing it matters more; do not stop at repetition.

examples.zh: 导师常说：照着讲，接着讲，传统才有生命力。
examples.en: My supervisor often says 'repeat, then continue', and only then does a tradition stay alive.

story.en: In the introduction to 'New Principle Learning' (《新理学》, 1939) Feng wrote that he was speaking 'in continuation of' (接着) Song-Ming Neo-Confucianism, not 'following' (照着) it.
story.zh: 冯友兰在《新理学》（1939年）绪论中说，他是“接着”宋明道学讲，而不是“照着”讲。

usage.en: Often quoted as 接着讲, 不是照着讲. Feng set out the distinction in the introduction to 《新理学》 (1939), saying his philosophy 'continues' Song-Ming Neo-Confucianism rather than 'follows' it. Used in academic and cultural discussion. Label set to republic-era for the 1939 origin, though quoted mostly in later decades.
usage.zh: 常简称“接着讲，不照着讲”。冯友兰在《新理学》（1939年）绪论中提出，称自己的哲学是“接着”宋明理学讲，而非“照着”讲。多见于学术和文化讨论。因出处在1939年，标为民国；后世引用更多。

meaning.en: Feng Youlan's scheme of four stages of spiritual outlook: the natural, the utilitarian, the moral and the cosmic (heaven-and-earth) level.
meaning.zh: 冯友兰提出的人生精神境界的四个层次：自然境界、功利境界、道德境界、天地境界。

equivalents: the four stages of life's outlook
four levels of spiritual awareness

examples.zh: 哲学课上讲了冯友兰的人生四境界。
examples.en: The philosophy class covered Feng Youlan's four levels of life.

examples.zh: 她在作文里用人生四境界来分析主人公的变化。
examples.en: In her essay she used the four levels of life to analyse the protagonist's change.

usage.en: A philosophical term, not a quotation; the four levels are 自然境界, 功利境界, 道德境界 and 天地境界. Not to be confused with 王国维's three stages (人生三境界). Common in school essays and philosophy courses.
usage.zh: 哲学术语，并非引语；四境界即自然、功利、道德、天地境界。不要与王国维的“人生三境界”混淆。常见于作文和哲学课程。

text: 上穷碧落下黄泉，动手动脚找东西
pinyin: shàng qióng bì luò xià huáng quán, dòng shǒu dòng jiǎo zhǎo dōng xī
literal: up · exhaust · azure · heaven down · yellow · springs, move · hands · move · feet · seek · things
natural: search the heavens above and the underworld below; use hands and feet to find things

meaning.en: Fu Sinian's motto for evidence-based research: go everywhere and dig up new material instead of relying on armchair argument.
meaning.zh: 傅斯年提倡的史学研究信条：上天入地、亲自动手去寻找新材料，而不是坐在书斋里空谈。

equivalents: leave no stone unturned
go out and find the evidence

examples.zh: 考古队的口号是“上穷碧落下黄泉，动手动脚找东西”。
examples.en: The archaeological team's motto is 'search heaven and the underworld, and go out to find things with your own hands'.

examples.zh: 做田野调查就要上穷碧落下黄泉，动手动脚找东西。
examples.en: Fieldwork means searching high and low and going out to find things yourself.

origin.source: 傅斯年《历史语言研究所工作之旨趣》（1928年）

story.en: Fu Sinian, founding director of the Institute of History and Philology (Academia Sinica), used the line in his 1928 founding statement, urging scholars to find new material.
story.zh: 1928年，史语所首任所长傅斯年在《历史语言研究所工作之旨趣》中提出此语，号召学者去寻找新材料。

usage.en: The first half borrows 白居易《长恨歌》: 上穷碧落下黄泉，两处茫茫皆不见. Fu's second half is a playful, down-to-earth twist. Quoted in history, archaeology and research settings.
usage.zh: 上半句取自白居易《长恨歌》“上穷碧落下黄泉，两处茫茫皆不见”，傅斯年续以通俗的下半句，风趣而务实。常见于历史学、考古学和研究场合。

text: 我爱咱们的国呀，可是谁爱我呢
pinyin: wǒ ài zán men de guó yā, kě shì shéi ài wǒ ne
literal: I · love · our · country · [exclamation], but · who · loves · me · [question]
natural: I love our country, but who loves me?

meaning.en: A bitter cry from Lao She's play Teahouse: an ordinary man loves his country but is let down by it.
meaning.zh: 老舍话剧《茶馆》中的悲愤之语：普通人热爱国家，却得不到国家的善待。

equivalents: I love my country, but does it love me back?
love unreturned

examples.zh: 看完《茶馆》，他想起那句“我爱咱们的国呀，可是谁爱我呢”。
examples.en: After seeing 'Teahouse' he thought of the line 'I love our country, but who loves me?'

examples.zh: 面对不公，他苦笑着说：“我爱咱们的国呀，可是谁爱我呢？”
examples.en: Faced with injustice he said with a wry smile, 'I love our country, but who loves me?'

story.en: Chang Siye, an honest Manchu bannerman, says the line in the last act of Lao She's play, set in a Beijing teahouse across three eras.
story.zh: 老舍话剧《茶馆》最后一幕，正直的旗人常四爷所说，剧情横跨三个时代。

usage.en: A quoted line spoken by the character Chang Siye (常四爷) in Act 3 of Lao She's 《茶馆》 (1957). Quoted with sadness or irony about being let down by one's country or institutions; patriotic feeling underlies it.
usage.zh: 引自老舍《茶馆》（1957年）第三幕，由常四爷说出。引用时带着悲愤或讽刺，表达对国家、制度未能善待自己的感慨，底色仍是爱国。

pinyin: zhè shì yī gōu jué wàng de sǐ shuǐ
literal: this · is · one · ditch · hopeless · [particle] · dead · water
natural: this is a ditch of hopeless dead water

meaning.en: The opening line of Wen Yiduo's poem 'Dead Water': a stagnant ditch that stands for a hopeless, decaying society.
meaning.zh: 闻一多诗《死水》开篇：一沟停滞不动的臭水，象征绝望、腐朽的社会。

equivalents: a stagnant pool of despair
a society gone stagnant

examples.zh: 他引用“这是一沟绝望的死水”来形容那个死气沉沉的小镇。
examples.en: He quoted 'this is a ditch of hopeless dead water' to describe the lifeless town.

examples.zh: 读完《死水》，同学们对“这是一沟绝望的死水”有了新的理解。
examples.en: After reading 'Dead Water', the students saw 'this is a ditch of hopeless dead water' in a new light.

origin.source: 闻一多《死水》（1925年作，1926年发表）

story.en: Wen Yiduo wrote the poem 'Dead Water' in 1925 and published it in 1926 in the Morning Post supplement; it became the title of his 1928 collection.
story.zh: 闻一多1925年作《死水》，1926年发表于《晨报诗镌》，后成为1928年诗集的书名。

usage.en: The first line of a poem often read as a lament on the old society. Quoted to describe stagnation and hopelessness; literary and a school-curriculum staple. The poem continues 清风吹不起半点漪沦.
usage.zh: 全诗首句，一般理解为对旧社会的悲叹。常用来形容停滞、绝望的状态；书面语，是中学课文常见内容。下一句是“清风吹不起半点漪沦”。

text: 我挥一挥衣袖，不带走一片云彩
pinyin: wǒ huī yī huī yī xiù, bù dài zǒu yī piàn yún cǎi
literal: I · wave · one · wave · sleeve, not · take · away · one · piece · cloud
natural: I wave my sleeve and take not one cloud away

meaning.en: A light, graceful farewell: leaving without taking or disturbing anything.
meaning.zh: 潇洒、轻盈的告别：离开时不带走、也不惊动任何东西。

equivalents: leave without a trace
take nothing, disturb nothing

examples.zh: 毕业典礼上，校长引用了“我挥一挥衣袖，不带走一片云彩”。
examples.en: At graduation the principal quoted 'I wave my sleeve and take not one cloud away'.

examples.zh: 他离职时只说了一句：“我挥一挥衣袖，不带走一片云彩。”
examples.en: On leaving he said only, 'I wave my sleeve and take not one cloud away'.

story.en: Xu Zhimo wrote 'Saying Goodbye to Cambridge' in November 1928, on the voyage home after revisiting the university; it appeared in the journal Crescent Moon (《新月》) that December.
story.zh: 徐志摩1928年11月重访剑桥后在归途中写成《再别康桥》，同年12月发表于《新月》。

usage.en: The last stanza of 《再别康桥》, and the best-known line of the poem. The first stanza is a separate entry: 轻轻的我走了，正如我轻轻的来；我轻轻的招手，作别西天的云彩. Literary; often quoted at partings and in resignation notes.
usage.zh: 《再别康桥》的末节，也是全诗最广为人知的一句。首节见另一词条：轻轻的我走了，正如我轻轻的来；我轻轻的招手，作别西天的云彩。书面语，常用于告别和辞职场合。

pinyin: zuì shì nà yī dī tóu de wēn róu
literal: most · is · that · one · lowering of head's · tenderness
natural: the loveliest thing is the tenderness of that bowed head

meaning.en: The gentle charm of a shy, lowered head; used for a quiet, tender moment.
meaning.zh: 那一低头的羞怯与温柔，形容含蓄动人的瞬间。

equivalents: the sweetness of a shy lowered head
tenderness in a single glance down

examples.zh: 最是那一低头的温柔，让他记了一辈子。
examples.en: 'The tenderness of that bowed head' stayed with him all his life.

examples.zh: 朋友圈配文写着：最是那一低头的温柔。
examples.en: The caption read: 'the loveliest thing is the tenderness of that bowed head'.

origin.source: 徐志摩《沙扬娜拉·赠日本女郎》（1924年）

story.en: Xu Zhimo wrote the sequence 'Sayonara: to a Japanese Girl' after accompanying Tagore on a visit to Japan in 1924; this is its last line group.
story.zh: 1924年徐志摩陪泰戈尔访日后写下《沙扬娜拉·赠日本女郎》组诗，此为其中最后一首的名句。

usage.en: A line from the poem 'Sayonara' (《沙扬娜拉》), written for a Japanese girl he met on a 1924 trip to Japan. The next line reads 像一朵水莲花不胜凉风的娇羞. Quoted for a shy, tender gesture, often of a woman; literary.
usage.zh: 出自诗《沙扬娜拉》（赠日本女郎），写于1924年访日期间。下一句是“像一朵水莲花不胜凉风的娇羞”。多用来形容含羞的温柔动作，常指女子；书面语。

text: 我将于茫茫人海中访我唯一灵魂之伴侣；得之，我幸；不得，我命
pinyin: wǒ jiāng yú máng máng rén hǎi zhōng fǎng wǒ wéi yī líng hún zhī bàn lǚ, dé zhī, wǒ xìng, bù dé, wǒ mìng
literal: I · shall · in · vast · sea of people · seek · my · only · soul's · companion; obtain · it, I · fortunate; not · obtain, I · fate
natural: I shall seek my one soul-mate in the vast sea of people; if found, I am fortunate; if not, it is my fate

meaning.en: A romantic creed: seek the one true soulmate; finding them is luck, missing them is fate.
meaning.zh: 一种爱情信条：在茫茫人海中寻找唯一的灵魂伴侣，找到是幸运，找不到是命运。

equivalents: seek your one true soulmate
if found, fortune; if not, fate

examples.zh: 他在日记里抄下“我将于茫茫人海中访我唯一灵魂之伴侣；得之，我幸；不得，我命”。
examples.en: In his diary he copied down 'I shall seek my one soul-mate in the vast sea of people; if found, I am fortunate; if not, it is my fate'.

examples.zh: 谈到婚恋观，她引用了“我将于茫茫人海中访我唯一灵魂之伴侣；得之，我幸；不得，我命”。
examples.en: Speaking of love and marriage she quoted 'I shall seek my one soul-mate in the vast sea of people…'.

origin.source: 徐志摩致梁启超信（1922年3月）

story.en: Xu Zhimo wrote to his teacher Liang Qichao, who had urged him to reconsider his divorce, explaining his search for a true soulmate in these words.
story.zh: 徐志摩写信给劝他慎重对待离婚的老师梁启超，用这几句话说明自己追求真正灵魂伴侣的心愿。

usage.en: From a letter to Liang Qichao (梁启超) of March 1922, written when Xu was pursuing a divorce; the letter continues 如此而已. Quoted in discussions of romantic ideals; literary, in classical-flavoured prose.
usage.zh: 出自1922年3月徐志摩致梁启超的信，当时他正在办理离婚；信中下接“如此而已”。常在谈论爱情理想时引用；书面语，带文言色彩。

text: 曾因酒醉鞭名马，生怕情多累美人
pinyin: céng yīn jiǔ zuì biān míng mǎ, shēng pà qíng duō lěi měi rén
literal: once · because · wine · drunk · whip · famous · horse, fear · feeling · much · burden · beauty
natural: once, drunk, I whipped a fine horse; I fear too much feeling might burden a beauty

meaning.en: A romantic, self-mocking couplet: a man who acts rashly when drunk but holds back in love for fear of hurting the woman.
meaning.zh: 带点自嘲的风流联句：酒后曾放纵不羁，却因怕深情拖累佳人而克制。

equivalents: reckless in wine, restrained in love
too tender-hearted to burden her

examples.zh: 他把“曾因酒醉鞭名马，生怕情多累美人”写在了扇面上。
examples.en: He wrote 'once, drunk, I whipped a fine horse…' on a fan.

examples.zh: 讲到郁达夫，老师念起“曾因酒醉鞭名马，生怕情多累美人”。
examples.en: Speaking of Yu Dafu, the teacher recited 'once, drunk, I whipped a fine horse; I fear too much feeling might burden a beauty'.

story.en: Yu Dafu wrote this poem on the wall of the Diaotai (Yan Ziling's fishing terrace) in 1931 and later included it in the essay 'A Spring Noon at Diaotai'.
story.zh: 1931年郁达夫在严子陵钓台题壁作此诗，后收入散文《钓台的春昼》。

usage.en: Yu Dafu's couplet in classical style, echoing earlier 'romantic wanderer' verse. Quoted for a scholar's mix of rashness and tenderness; literary.
usage.zh: 郁达夫的旧体诗联，带有传统才子风流的意味。常用来形容文人既放浪又多情的性格；书面语。

pinyin: jiāo shì wèi le bù jiāo
literal: teaching · is · for · the sake of · not · teaching
natural: teaching is so that one need not teach

meaning.en: Ye Shengtao's principle of education: teach so well that students learn to learn by themselves, and eventually need no teacher.
meaning.zh: 叶圣陶的教育主张：教学的目的是让学生学会自学，最终不再需要教。

equivalents: teach so that they can learn without you
the aim of teaching is independence

examples.zh: 叶圣陶说，教是为了不教，要培养学生自学的能力。
examples.en: Ye Shengtao said teaching aims at not needing to teach: build students' ability to study alone.

examples.zh: 她的教学理念就是“教是为了不教”。
examples.en: Her teaching philosophy is 'teaching is so that one need not teach'.

origin.source: 叶圣陶教育论述（20世纪60年代起）

story.en: Ye Shengtao, writer and educator, repeatedly stated this principle from the early 1960s, notably in 'Study Chinese Seriously' (1962).
story.zh: 作家、教育家叶圣陶自1960年代初起多次阐述此主张，如《认真学习语文》（1962年）。

usage.en: A compact form of Ye Shengtao's saying that 'the aim of teaching is to reach the point of not needing to teach' (教是为了达到不需要教). The shortened wording is the popular one; the exact date of its first use is not verified, so it is usually dated to the 1960s-80s. Common in education writing.
usage.zh: 是叶圣陶“教是为了达到不需要教”的简缩说法，流传的是简缩形式，最初使用时间未核实，一般系于1960至80年代。常见于教育类文章。

text: 准备着明天就死，工作着仿佛永远活着
pinyin: zhǔn bèi zhe míng tiān jiù sǐ, gōng zuò zhe fǎng fú yǒng yuǎn huó zhe
literal: prepare · [particle] · tomorrow · then · die, work · [particle] · as if · forever · live · [particle]
natural: be ready to die tomorrow, yet work as if you will live forever

meaning.en: A life motto: stay ready for death at any moment, but work with the steadiness of one who has all the time in the world.
meaning.zh: 一种人生信条：随时做好离世的准备，工作时却像永远不会死去一样踏实投入。

equivalents: live each day as if it were your last, work as if you will live forever
be ready for the end, work without end

examples.zh: 他把“准备着明天就死，工作着仿佛永远活着”写在了办公桌前。
examples.en: He wrote 'be ready to die tomorrow, yet work as if you will live forever' above his desk.

examples.zh: 采访中，老科学家说起“准备着明天就死，工作着仿佛永远活着”。
examples.en: In the interview the old scientist spoke of being ready to die tomorrow while working as if living forever.

origin.source: 传为丁文江语（出处待考）

story.en: Attributed to Ding Wenjiang, the geologist and founder of the Geological Survey of China; where he said or wrote it is unverified.
story.zh: 传为中国地质调查所创办人、地质学家丁文江所说；其说出或写下的场合未经核实。

usage.en: Attributed to the geologist Ding Wenjiang (丁文江), a friend of Hu Shi, who is said to have lived by it; the exact source and wording are not verified (it resembles a saying often credited to others), so the entry gives no origin text beyond the attribution.
usage.zh: 传为地质学家丁文江（胡适之友）的座右铭；确切出处和措辞未核实（与常被归于他人的一句名言相似），故仅注明传说归属。

meaning.en: The title of Qu Qiubai's reflective memoir written in prison in 1935, shortly before his execution; now a symbol of candid self-examination.
meaning.zh: 瞿秋白1935年被捕后在狱中写下的自述的题目，不久后他就义；今天是坦率自省的象征。

equivalents: superfluous words
a candid last testament

examples.zh: 读完《多余的话》，他对瞿秋白有了更复杂的看法。
examples.en: After reading 'Superfluous Words' he saw Qu Qiubai in a more complex light.

examples.zh: 这篇回忆录坦率得像一篇“多余的话”。
examples.en: The memoir is as candid as a set of 'superfluous words'.

usage.en: Mostly met as a title; 《多余的话》 was written in June 1935 in a Nationalist prison and has been debated for decades because of its frank self-doubt. Not a quotation, so no famous-quotes label.
usage.zh: 主要作为书名出现。《多余的话》1935年6月写于国民党狱中，因其坦率的自我怀疑而讨论多年。并非引语，故不加名人名言标签。
